text:
The Rangers' crease has been the loudest thing about them all week. James Reimer went on unconditional waivers for a contract termination, Joonas Korpisalo won his season debut in Seattle on Saturday, and tonight the net goes back to Dylan Garand, whose name has been in more headlines over the last two weeks than any other Ranger. He has earned the attention the right way: a .906 save rate and +2.2 goals saved above expected (saves beyond what the shot quality predicts) in 13 games. New York arrives on a three-game winning streak, and the chances back it, 60% of the expected goals across those three.

Edmonton counters with Devon Levi, activated off injured reserve on Saturday and sitting at .888 and -1.1 this season. That's the matchup inside the matchup. The Oilers have 27 points and are running hot, a +21 goal difference built on +5.4 expected; finishing has done most of the lifting. Connor McDavid brings an 18-game point streak (10 goals, 37 assists), Leon Draisaitl has goals in three straight, and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins is good to go tonight, per CBS Sports.

Our numbers don't buy the 4-1 Edmonton win in New York on Nov 1 as the whole story. At five on five the Rangers have taken 52% of the expected goals, Edmonton 49%, and the Oilers take 4.1 penalties a game. We have New York at 48% to win, well above DraftKings' 41%. The Rangers are missing Sean Durzi and Alberts Smits on the back end, which has pushed Adam Fox to 24:32 a night.

The question for the Rangers is simple: can Garand keep doing this against the two best forwards he will see all month? If he can, a team our playoff odds have at 55% banks the kind of road win that changes a week.
headline: Garand gets the net, and McDavid's streak comes with it

hunch.text: Our gut agrees with our numbers more than the market does: the Rangers' chances have been real for a week, Levi is just off injured reserve, and we think New York steals this one.
